name: AI UI Style Vault 3D Mode Classification
purpose: Classify an already-justified 3D request by interaction mode before choosing asset production or browser runtime. Asset format never determines the mode by itself.
hardRules: Classify from the verified user goal and required interaction, not from visual novelty or file extension.
A GLB/GLTF asset never automatically implies user-controlled rotation.
If 3D does not materially improve comprehension, inspection, configuration, navigation or storytelling, return mode 0 (none).
Use the lowest-complexity mode that fully satisfies the user goal.
Modes 3-6 require real or clearly approved 3D geometry; CSS pseudo-3D and video are not substitutes for user-controlled geometry.
Modes 3-4 require stable bounded manipulation, reset/recenter and touch/keyboard-accessible alternatives.
Modes 5-6 require explicit navigation/camera bounds and stronger performance/fallback planning.
The selected mode does not bypass subject relevance, provenance, accessibility, performance or runtime validation gates.

modes.label: No 3D
modes.summary: Use normal DOM, imagery, illustration or video because real-time 3D adds no material user value.
examples: service website where a diagram explains the process better than 3D
avoid: adding WebGL only to look premium

modes.label: 3D Visual Only
modes.summary: Use depth, perspective or a rendered 3D subject as authored visual composition with no direct object manipulation.
examples: fashion hero with a floating shoe that follows an authored pose but cannot be freely rotated
avoid: claiming a visual-only scene is a product inspector

modes.label: Authored 3D Animation
modes.summary: Use a controlled timeline, camera path or model animation where the visitor observes or scroll-scrubs an authored sequence rather than freely manipulating the subject.
examples: dress rotates automatically during a cinematic campaign section but users do not control the angle
avoid: using autoplay motion when the actual goal is product inspection

modes.label: Inspectable 3D Object
modes.summary: Let the visitor directly inspect one bounded object using rotate/orbit, drag/swipe, zoom, presets or verified hotspots.
examples: 3D mannequin wearing a dress that users can swipe or drag to inspect 360 degrees
avoid: free-flight controls around a small product
auto-rotation as the only inspection method

modes.label: Configurable 3D Object
modes.summary: Let the visitor inspect an object and change verified variants, materials, components, states or options that materially affect the represented product.
examples: mannequin dress viewer where customers rotate the look and switch only between actual available fabrics or colours
avoid: treating decorative colour changes as commerce truth

modes.label: Spatial Exploration
modes.summary: Let the visitor navigate or move between meaningful places, rooms, stations, exhibits or spatial nodes where understanding location and relationship is part of the task.
examples: walk through a verified apartment or fashion showroom and move between rooms/stations
avoid: unbounded fly mode when guided nodes are clearer

modes.label: Interactive 3D World
modes.summary: Use a custom real-time scene with multiple independently interactive objects, game-like logic, physics, deep simulation or large spatial/data systems.
examples: interactive virtual fashion world with multiple mannequins, character navigation and object interactions
avoid: using this mode for a single rotatable product
adding physics without a user-task reason

assetFormatPolicy.rule: Asset format confirms feasibility after mode selection; it must not upgrade the selected mode.
examples: A GLB used only in a cinematic hero can remain authored-animation or visual-only.
A request for 360 drag/swipe inspection requires inspectable-object even when no GLB exists yet; missing geometry routes to production-resource intelligence.
A building GLB does not make a walkthrough a model-viewer task; spatial-exploration still requires a custom spatial runtime.
